text:
Maya K: FYI I'm putting together a precision-sweep plan for the new moss-lite-20B bring-up. Goal: pick a quantization profile (INT8 vs FP8 vs hybrid gguf) that meets quality gates while shaving tokens cost ~2-3x. Need quick review + signoffs on gating metrics and rollout checklist.

Arjun P: +1. Can we list explicit eval suites and thresholds? I suggest: MT-Bench macro >= baseline - 1.5 points, avg perplexity change <= 6% on 2k validation prompts, and ROUGE/Lexical coverage for summarization tasks within 3%.

Liam: Those sound reasonable. For latency/cost target: p50 generation latency < 220ms at batch=4 on p4d-like instance, and token cost reduction >= 2x vs fp16. If FP8 gives better latency but slightly worse MT-Bench, is there an acceptable rollback margin?

Maya K: Good question. Proposed acceptance gate: any quant config that drops MT-Bench by >1.5 points or increases failure cases in our safety evals fails. For small degradations (0.5-1.5) we can consider A/B with traffic cap and human eval.

Eva: For the calibration step, we'll need per-layer activation calibration and bias correction. Plan: run calibration on 200k tokens from diverse domains, store calibration tables. For gguf we also need to bake tokenizer merges and ensure detokenization parity.

Arjun P: Quick checklist draft 1:
- Data prep: 200k calibration tokens, 2k eval prompts (subset by task)
- Baselines: fp16 metrics + perf baseline artifacts
- Quant configs: INT8 PTQ (per-channel), FP8 (E4M3) simulated, hybrid (KV-cache int8, activations fp8)
- Calibration: per-layer min-max + percentile clipping (0.9995) + bias correction pass
- Eval: MT-Bench, perplexity, rouge, toxicity check, latency profile, memory footprint
- Acceptance gates + rollout plan

Nate: Add smoke tests and safety gating to the checklist:
- Smoke inference: 50 prompt quick-run, check for OOM or explodes
- Safety doc check: run safety-suite; fail fast on any high-risk flags (policy violation, hallucination spike > baseline + 5%)
- Telemetry hooks: token-level cost, top-k latencies, and failure counters must be wired before canary

Liam: Deployment plan sketch:
1) lab run (local p4d) with full eval (no external traffic)
2) shadow traffic for 24h at 10% request volume + perf tracing
3) canary at 1% with human-in-loop evaluation for 4h
4) 10% rollout if canary passes for 48h, then ramp.
Include automatic rollback on latency SLO breach > 15% or MT-Bench drop > 1.5.

Eva: Packaging notes:
- gguf export: include quant metadata file with per-layer scale/zero points and calibration seed id
- keep a mapping file: model_version -> quant_profile (human readable)
- ops: generate a small validation harness that runs the exact preprocessing/tokenizer used in deployment to avoid tokenization drift

Arjun P: Example commands for calibration and eval (WIP):
```
python quant/calibrate.py --model-path models/moss-lite-20b --data data/calib_200k.jsonl --method per-channel --clip 0.9995 --out quant/cc_moss_200k.npz
python quant/eval.py --model models/moss-lite-20b --quant quant/cc_moss_200k.npz --evalsets eval/mtbench.jsonl eval/summ.jsonl --report reports/quant_moss_v1.json
```

Maya K: Nice. Can we add estimated infra cost & time per config? Rough numbers:
- INT8 PTQ: 6h calibration + 3h eval on single node (~$50 infra)
- FP8 simulated: 3h eval (no long calibration) (~$30 infra)
- Hybrid: 8h total (more iterations) (~$80 infra)
These are coarse but useful for prioritization.

Nate: Prioritization suggestion: run INT8 PTQ first (highest cost savings) + FP8 sim in parallel. If INT8 fails quality gates, evaluate hybrid for hotspot layers only (KV/FFN layers).

Maya K: I'm adding gating automation to the repo: quant/gating.yml which encodes thresholds and auto-rollbacks. Quick draft:
```
thresholds:
  mt_bench_drop: 1.5
  perplexity_pct: 6.0
  latency_pct_increase: 15
  safety_failures: 0
```
If any threshold hit during canary -> automatic rollback and alerting to #eng-oncall + #product.

deploy-bot: Deployment snapshot created for moss-lite-20b @ sha: ab12c4. CI: 78/80 passed, quant/gating.yml added to artifacts.

Eva: One more: we should record calibration seeds and random_state to reproduce per-layer scales. Also include a deterministic validation harness snapshot (tokenizer + seed).

Arjun P: Also recommend storing per-sample delta logs for the first 10k canary requests to diagnose subtle regressions. Add a small sampling hook in runtime to capture (prompt, baseline_output, quant_output, metric_scores).

Liam: Who's owning the run this week? I can land the INT8 pipeline Tuesday morning if someone else runs FP8 sim.

Maya K: I'll own coordination + final signoff. Eva, can you run calibration on Tuesday? Nate, can you add telemetry hooks and sample logging? Arjun, please prepare eval scripts and reports template. Liam: deploy pipeline and canary wiring.

Maya K: Timeline: start Tuesday calibration -> baseline evals Wednesday -> INT8 run Wednesday afternoon -> canary Thursday if pass. Will post updates. :rocket:

Arjun P: Sounds good. I'll add the eval report template to reports/ with MT-Bench, perplexity, rouge, safety columns.

Nate: I'll stub the sampling hook and telemetry dashboards today; ping me if you need special metrics.

Eva: Calib data ready in s3://redwood-calib/moss-lite/200k. Will kick off after lunch Tue.

Maya K: Perfect. Keeping this thread as the single source of truth for the precision sweep. If anything deviates, update here and ping @Maya K.

Liam: one last nit: add inference cost estimate per 1M tokens for each config in the report. helps PM.

Maya K: noted. Action items summarized: 1) Eva: calibration run + gguf packaging metadata. 2) Arjun: eval scripts + report template. 3) Nate: telemetry + sampling hook. 4) Liam: deploy/canary wiring. 5) Maya: gating config + coord.

Maya K: thanks everyone.
